_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for disjoint-sets.

questions.title: Group representative
questions.code:
parent:
A -> A
B -> A
C -> C

find(B) follows B -> A
questions.prompt: In a disjoint set, what does find(x) return?
choices: The smallest value in the whole input
The number of edges in a graph
The next item in a queue
questions.explanation: Find returns the representative used to compare whether two values belong to the same group.

questions.title: Union meaning
questions.code:
Before union(A, C):
group 1: A, B
group 2: C

After union(A, C):
one group: A, B, C
choices: Merge the groups containing a and b
Delete a and b from memory
Create a directed edge from a to b only
questions.explanation: Union connects the two sets at the group level, even if a and b are not the current representatives.

questions.title: Connected check
questions.prompt: After union(A, B) and union(B, C), what should find(A) == find(C) report?
questions.explanation: A connects to B and B connects to C, so all three values end up in one component.

questions.title: Path compression
questions.prompt: Why use path compression after find?
questions.explanation: Path compression points visited nodes closer to the representative without changing which group they are in.

questions.title: Union by size
questions.prompt: Why attach the smaller group under the larger group?
choices: It forces every group size to one
questions.explanation: Rank or size keeps the parent tree shallow when groups merge. Shallow trees make later find calls reach the representative with fewer steps.

questions.title: Cycle detection
questions.prompt: When processing an undirected edge (u, v), what suggests the edge creates a cycle?
choices: u and v already have the same representative
u and v are different strings
The graph has no edges yet
questions.explanation: If both endpoints are already in one component, adding another edge between them creates a cycle.

questions.title: Component count
questions.prompt: When should the component count decrease?
choices: When union merges two different groups
When a duplicate union is ignored
questions.explanation: The component count changes only when two different groups merge. If both values already have the same representative, the link does not reduce the count.

questions.title: Union mistake
questions.prompt: What is a common disjoint-set bug?
choices: Comparing parent values before calling find
Initializing each item as its own parent
questions.explanation: A parent pointer may point to an intermediate node, not the final representative. Calling find first gives the group representative that should be compared.
